text: How do I pursue life goals while married to a struggling spouse? The guy is 50 years old, male, and the woman is 44 years old, female. Wife Kelly, 44, and I, 50 years old, have been married 10 years and have two elementary age kids. A year ago, Kelly was caught sleeping with her co-worker by the co-worker's girlfriend. Kelly went to counseling and later admitted it was her third affair, but the only one that became physical. Kelly is reliant upon me for financial support. Through intense therapy, she learned that she is bipolar. She's also ADHD and struggles with alcohol addiction, going in and out of AA, so that's anonymous alcoholics, I believe, several times throughout our 10-year marriage. She typically doesn't drink, but I recently learned that she occasionally drinks with friends when I'm not around. She continues to be a chronic liar, lying about mostly little things that don't really matter. Three years ago, she was caught shoplifting at her local grocery. Kelly appears to be a typical suburban mother and wife, but has deep, dark struggles that most people don't know about because her exterior is very happy and bubbly. Because of ADHD, she doesn't complete tasks and doesn't show up for many household responsibilities. She still works with her fair partner, with her fair part, probably, and we are really in our third week of marriage counseling because she kept putting it off. I am ready to move forward and continue pursuing my life goals, financial, home, fitness, parenting, spousal, etc. I am struggling to figure out if I can pursue these things while still married to Kelly. I want to start by saying that for some people, the only thing that grows with age is the number of years, not wisdom or experience. This is exactly where your life can end up if you keep making bad decisions, if you don't learn, if you don't respect yourself, and if you let someone treat you like a doormat. This man is 50 years old. His wife has cheated on him at least three times, probably more. She lies constantly. She drinks. She's been in and out of AA, got caught shoplifting, has mental health issues, doesn't pull her weight at home, and on top of all that, she's financially dependent on him. Fantastic choice of a partner, right? Even one of those things would be enough reason to run, but all of them combined, you should be sprinting away from her like she's on fire. Drop everything, divorce, try not to have anything with this person anymore. Of course, you have kids, so probably you wouldn't be able to end all of the interactions, but if, for example, after the divorce, you won't be able to keep the kids with you, just limit interactions strictly about kids. And yeah, you are 50. If you haven't grown a backbone by now, it's hard to believe you'll suddenly develop one, but better late than never. Start turning your life around. Dig up whatever dignity and self-respect you've still got left, if there's any. Work on yourself. Fix your mindset, and maybe you still have a chance. And for everyone watching, understand this, wrong actions lead to wrong consequences. If you don't set standards, if you don't demand respect, you can end up in the same miserable place as this guy.
